review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result
item.description: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected; wrapping the result in ledgerly.money.round_money fixed it.
item.content: Before writing any function that produces a money value, check the repo's money module for a canonical rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and apply it to the final result. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and violate the team convention.

item.title: Read the money module and existing sibling functions before implementing
item.description: The agent only discovered round_money, ZERO, and to_money after the review; inspecting money.py and invoice_total/line_total upfront would have avoided the rejection.
item.content: When adding a function to a module, first read the module's imports and neighboring functions to learn the established patterns (rounding, zero constants, type coercion). Mirror those patterns in the new code.

item.title: Handle the empty/zero-denominator case explicitly
item.description: Returning ZERO when total_quantity is 0 satisfies the spec's 'invoice without lines has an average of zero' requirement and avoids division by zero.
item.content: For weighted-average or ratio computations, guard the denominator before dividing and return the domain's zero constant (e.g. ZERO) rather than raising or returning a float 0.
